title: Post-archive hosted functional recovery
outOfScope: Release publication, version/tag changes, and modifying archived Contract, Summary, Outcome, or manifest evidence.
Changing normal PR aggregate ownership, coverage thresholds, test selection, or the existing historical-preservation predicate.

sources.reason: Hosted functional recovery currently requires a narrow marker that a normal failed pytest job does not emit.
Existing provider-bound recovery tests establish the receipt and validation boundary.
Hosted project-test-lifecycle failure proves the marker mismatch and preserves red failure evidence.
User-approved cleanup issue and human authority reference.

riskAssessment.reason: Recovery receipts authorize post-archive changes; accepting an unbound or non-functional provider failure could let unrelated changes enter an already archived Work Item.
riskAssessment.unknownsReviewEvidence: The failed lifecycle shard, its uploaded JUnit/receipt artifacts, and the existing marker-only validator identify the required narrow condition.

reasons: Post-archive recovery changes require strict audit, source binding, and failure preservation.

override.reason: Strict corrective review for append-only recovery evidence; release operations are excluded.
notRunChecks: Release checks are inapplicable because this Work Item does not change release-owned resources.

executionDecision.reason: The user approved this one corrective Work Item and the exact hosted failure provides the evidence-bound scope.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A completed provider-bound pull-request job with a failed pytest/JUnit functional result can create an append-only same-Work-Item recovery receipt without requiring an incidental marker string.
The receipt still binds repository, PR, candidate SHA, completed failed run/job, workflow path, log digest, archive digests, human authority, and explicitly listed recovery paths.
Coverage-shortfall recovery remains separately classified and arbitrary failed-log text or success/cancelled/wrong-SHA provider facts remain rejected.
Focused tests demonstrate the previously rejected standard pytest failure is accepted and negative provider bindings fail closed.
The recovery lifecycle documentation describes the supported provider-bound functional failure evidence and its limitations.
guidelines: Keep post-archive recovery append-only and never mutate archived evidence.
Require provider-bound identity and a concrete failed functional test signal before authorizing any recovery path.
Do not publish releases or relax quality, coverage, or ownership gates.

intent.problem: A real hosted project-test-lifecycle pytest failure revealed a stale generated capability matrix, but the same-Work-Item recovery command rejects that evidence because it only recognizes a special marker absent from ordinary pytest/JUnit failures. That leaves a valid, narrow remediation path unable to be authorized.
constraints: Start from latest origin/main and keep this corrective Work Item independent of the archived cleanup branch.
Preserve all archived evidence and failed hosted artifacts without rewriting them.
Accept only provider-bound completed failed pull-request jobs with a canonical functional-test failure signal.
Retain separate coverage recovery and reject unbound, successful, cancelled, or arbitrary-log failures.
Do not release, change versions/tags, weaken quality gates, or add unrelated cleanup.
intent.rationale: Extending the existing provider binding to recognize canonical pytest/JUnit failure evidence restores the intended same-Work-Item recovery route while keeping its eligibility rule as narrow and auditable as the existing coverage route.

rawUserRequest: User authorized one necessary corrective Work Item to repair the post-archive hosted functional recovery mechanism and continue cleanup to completion.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair the narrow provider-bound functional-failure recovery classification without changing the normal quality or release paths.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A completed provider-bound pull-request job reports a real pytest/JUnit failure.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A functional-failure receipt binds the exact provider and archive facts and grants ownership only to listed recovery paths.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused recovery unit tests use a canonical pytest failure log and validate the emitted receipt offline.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A provider job is successful, cancelled, wrong-SHA, or has arbitrary error text without a canonical test failure.
scenarioCoverage.expected: No functional recovery receipt is created.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused negative tests mutate provider facts and logs, asserting fail-closed errors.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user explicitly authorized the single corrective Work Item after the hosted failure exposed the post-archive recovery mechanism gap.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
